title: Reflexive Verbs
description: Master reflexive verbs (levantarse, ducharse, sentirse) and pronoun usage in Spanish.

grammar.title: Reflexive Pronouns and Verb Conjugation
grammar.content:
Reflexive verbs indicate the action is performed by the subject on itself.

Reflexive pronouns:
me (myself)
te (yourself informal)
se (himself/herself/yourself formal)
nos (ourselves)
os (yourselves informal Spain)
se (themselves/yourselves formal)

Position: BEFORE the conjugated verb, or attached to the infinitive:
Me levanto. (I get up.)
Voy a ducharme. (I'm going to shower.)

In present tense:
Me levanto. (I get up.)
Te levantas. (You get up.)
Se levanta. (He/She gets up.)
Nos levantamos. (We get up.)
Os levantais. (You all get up, Spain.)
Se levantan. (They get up.)

In preterite:
Me levante. (I got up.)
Se levantó. (He/She got up.)
examples: Me ducho todas las mananas. (I shower every morning.)
A que hora te despiertas? (What time do you wake up?)
Nos vestimos rapido. (We get dressed quickly.)

grammar.title: Daily Routine with Reflexive Verbs
grammar.content:
Typical daily routine reflexive verbs:

Morning routine:
Me despierto a las siete. (I wake up at seven.)
Me levanto inmediatamente. (I get up immediately.)
Me ducho con agua fria. (I shower with cold water.)
Me lavo los dientes. (I brush my teeth.)
Me peino el pelo. (I comb my hair.)
Me visto. (I get dressed.)

Evening routine:
Me deshago la cama. (I make the bed.) → actually: Hacer la cama (to make the bed)
Me como. → This is NOT reflexive! Comerse is for eating with emphasis.
Me acuesto a las once. (I go to bed at eleven.)
Me duermo rapido. (I fall asleep quickly.)

Note: Body parts use definite article, not possessive:
Me lavo las manos. (I wash my hands.) — NOT 'mis manos'
examples: A que hora te despiertas? (What time do you wake up?)\nMe despierto a las 7. (I wake up at 7.)
Primero me ducho y luego me visto. (First I shower and then I get dressed.)
Me acuesto muy tarde los fines de semana. (I go to bed very late on weekends.)

grammar.title: Emotional and Mental State Reflexive Verbs
grammar.content:
Psychological/emotional reflexive verbs:

Sentir(sentirse) - to feel:
Me siento bien. (I feel well.)
Te sientes triste? (Do you feel sad?)
Se siente solo. (He feels lonely.)

Encontrarse - to feel (state):
Me encuentro mal. (I feel sick.)
Te encuentras mejor? (Do you feel better?)

Other emotional reflexives:
Me alegro de verte. (I'm glad to see you.)
Se preocupó mucho. (He worried a lot.)
Nos aburrimos en la fiesta. (We got bored at the party.)
Se enfado conmigo. (He got angry with me.)

Non-reflexive vs reflexive:
Aburrí a todos. (I bored everyone.) vs. Me aburro. (I get bored.)
Preocupo a mi madre. (I worry my mother.) vs. Me preocupo. (I worry.)
examples: Como te sientes? (How do you feel?)\nMe siento cansado. (I feel tired.)
Me alegro de que hayas venido. (I'm glad you came.)
No te preocupes por eso. (Don't worry about that.)
Nos divertimos mucho en el concierto. (We had a lot of fun at the concert.)

pronunciation.title: Reflexive Verbs Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Reflexive pronouns are unstressed, so they blend with the verb:

me = meh
te = teh
se = seh
nos = nos
os = os (Spain)
se = seh

When attached to infinitive/gerund, they form one word:
levantarse = leh-ban-TAR-seh
ducharse = doo-CHAR-seh
despertarse = des-pehr-TAR-seh

With conjugated verb (pronoun before):
Me levanto. (meh leh-VAN-toh)
Te duchas. (teh DOO-chahs)
Se levanta. (seh leh-VAN-tah)

Preterite reflexive:
Me levanté. (meh leh-van-TEH) — accent appears on verb
Se duchó. (seh doo-CHO) — accent on pronoun
examples: Me ducho. = meh DOO-choh\nTe levantas. = teh leh-VAN-tahs\nSe acuesta. = seh ah-KWES-tah

exercises.question: What is the correct reflexive form of 'I wake up' in present tense?
exercises.explanation: Me despierto = I wake up. Reflexive pronoun 'me' comes before the conjugated verb.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ ducho todas las mananas. (I shower every morning.)'
exercises.explanation: Me ducho = I shower. Reflexive verb ducharse requires 'me' pronoun.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I get dressed' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Vestirse is reflexive: 'Yo me visto' = I get dressed.

exercises.question: Complete: 'A que hora te ___? (What time do you wake up?)'
exercises.explanation: Despertarse = to wake up. 'Te despiertas' = you wake up (informal).

exercises.question: Which is correct: 'I brush my teeth' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Body parts use definite article, not possessive: 'Me cepillo los dientes' = I brush my teeth.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Me ___ bien hoy. (I feel good today.)'
exercises.explanation: Sentirse = to feel. 'Me siento bien' = I feel good/well.

exercises.question: How do you say 'We had fun' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Divertirse = to have fun. 'Nos divertimos' = We had fun (past tense).

exercises.question: Complete: 'No te ___ por eso. (Don't worry about that.)'
exercises.explanation: Preocuparse = to worry. In negative command: 'No te preocupes' = Don't worry.

exercises.question: What does 'Me acuesto' mean?
exercises.explanation: Acostarse = to go to bed. 'Me acuesto' = I go to bed / I lie down.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ellos se ___ muy Contentos. (They felt very happy.)'
exercises.explanation: Sentirse in preterite: 'Se sintieron' = They felt. 'Sintieron' is the preterite form.
